transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Yeah, um… I came in because I just can’t seem to be still. It’s like I got a motor running inside me all day, like my body is always telling me to move, even when I’m supposed to be sitting quiet.

Like at church, I try to sit there and listen, but after a little bit I feel trapped in the seat. Same thing here at the clinic, waiting around, or even just being at home. I’ll tell myself, “Just sit down, just relax,” but I can’t really do it. I gotta get up, walk around, mess with something, do something with my hands, anything. It feels real uncomfortable, like pressure building up inside me if I don’t move. That’s the main reason I’m here, because it’s been bothering me a lot.
You mentioned feeling restless in church, at the clinic, and at home. Do you also feel this way in other places, like at work or school, or when you're out with friends?

Yeah, I mean… I notice it most in places where I’m expected to sit still, like church, here at the clinic, or even at home when I’m supposed to just sit down and relax. It’s like my body doesn’t know how to just be quiet. I feel kind of trapped in the chair, like there’s this motor inside me running all day, and after a little bit I have to get up or do something with my hands.

Even if nothing is really happening, I’ll be sitting there thinking, “Okay, just stay put,” but then that restless feeling builds up and I end up moving around. So yeah, it’s not just one place—it follows me around. It’s real uncomfortable.
Do you feel this restlessness even when you're not anxious or worried about anything?

Yeah, yeah, I do. It’s not always because I’m worried about something. That’s what makes it kind of frustrating, because sometimes nothing bad is happening, nobody’s bothering me, I’m not sitting there thinking about some problem or anything like that… but my body still feels like it’s running.

Like at church, I might actually be trying to pay attention, just sitting there, and then after a little while it’s like I feel trapped in the seat. Same kind of thing here at the clinic, just waiting, or even at home where there’s no reason I should feel worked up. I’ll be sitting there and it’s like there’s a motor inside me that won’t shut off, and I have to get up, walk around, or do something with my hands.

So it’s not only when I’m anxious. It’s just there a lot of the time, like my body doesn’t know how to be still.
Do you also feel a sense of inner tension or mental restlessness, like your mind is racing or you just can’t relax inside, even if you’re not moving?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, it’s hard for me to separate it, you know? Because even if I’m sitting still on the outside for a minute, inside I still feel like I got that motor running. Like my body might be in the chair, but I don’t feel settled.

At church, for example, I’ll be sitting there trying to be respectful and listen, and I can feel this thing building in me, like I’m trapped in the seat. It’s not always like a thought racing about one thing, it’s more like I just can’t relax inside. Same here at the clinic, sitting and waiting, I start feeling like I need to get up, move around, touch something, do something with my hands. Even at home, where I should be able to just sit down and be comfortable, I still get that feeling like I can’t stay put.

So yeah, even before I move, there’s this restless feeling inside me. Like I’m wound up, and if I don’t get up or do something, it just gets more uncomfortable.
Have there been times when you felt unusually excited, energized, or like your thoughts were racing so fast you couldn’t keep up with them?

Um… unusually excited or energized? I don’t know if I’d call it that. I mean, I get restless and wound up, like I’ve been saying, but not really like I’m in some great mood or full of big energy where I feel different from myself.

As for thoughts racing… sometimes my mind doesn’t feel settled, but I’m not sure it’s like my thoughts are going so fast I can’t keep up with them. It’s more like I can’t relax, you know? Like I feel uncomfortable sitting there. But “unusually excited” or my thoughts flying that fast… I can’t really say I’ve noticed that, no.
Do you find it hard to focus or concentrate on things, like reading, watching TV, or following conversations, even when you're not moving around?

Yeah, I do. Even if I’m sitting still and not moving around, I can have a hard time keeping with what somebody’s saying. Like I’ll start out listening good, I really will, and I’ll be trying to follow it, but then somewhere in the middle my mind just kind of slips off.

It happens with regular stuff I need to know, too. Like if somebody’s talking through ride times — who’s picking up who, what time we’re leaving, where I’m supposed to be — I’ll hear the first part, and then I miss a piece, and then I’m confused later. Same with pantry lists, like if someone’s telling me what needs to be picked up or what’s already there, I’ll think I got it, but then I realize I missed some of it. Or church plans, when people are explaining what’s going on, what time something starts, who’s doing what… I’m listening at first, but after a bit I lose pieces I really needed.

And it’s frustrating because it’s not always like I’m walking around or doing something else. I can be right there looking at the person, trying to listen, and still it doesn’t all stay with me.
Do you often find that you’re not paying close attention to details, or do you make careless mistakes because your mind is somewhere else?

I’m not really sure about that one. I mean, I can say I miss things sometimes, but whether it’s because I’m not paying close attention to details or because my mind is somewhere else… I don’t know if I could separate that out real clear.

Like, if somebody later says, “You didn’t notice that part,” or “That’s not what I said,” I might realize I missed something, but I don’t always know in the moment what happened. I don’t sit there thinking, “Oh, I’m ignoring the details.” It’s more after the fact that I might see I didn’t catch everything.

As far as careless mistakes, I don’t know. I don’t have a good example coming to mind right now. I’m not saying it never happens, but I haven’t really paid attention to it that way, like enough to say yes, that’s a big thing for me.
Can you tell me if you also have trouble staying focused or feel restless in settings like work, school, or when you’re out with friends, even if you’re not moving around?

Yeah… that’s actually kind of the main reason I came in, to be honest. It’s like I’ve got a motor running inside me all day. That’s the best way I can explain it. Even if I’m sitting there and I’m not supposed to be doing anything, inside I don’t feel still. I feel like I need to get up, or shift around, or go do something, or I’m just… stuck in my own skin, if that makes sense.

Like at church, if I have to sit through everything, I start feeling trapped. Not because anything bad is happening, but because sitting there that long feels almost unbearable sometimes. Same thing at the clinic, like waiting around, sitting in the chair, trying to just be patient — I can do it for a little while, but then I start feeling like I’ve got to stand up or move or find some reason to do something.

And at home too, it’s not like it only happens out in public. If I’m just sitting there and I’m supposed to relax, I don’t really relax. I’ll feel that pressure inside, like I need to get up. Even if I’m not physically running around, I still feel restless inside. That’s probably the biggest thing — I don’t feel settled.
When did you first start noticing these feelings of restlessness and trouble focusing? Were they present when you were a child, or did they start more recently?

Yeah, it was definitely there when I was a kid. I don’t think this is something that just started recently. I mean, it feels worse now in some ways because I’m older and there’s more I’m supposed to handle, but when I think back, it was already happening when I was a boy in school.

Teachers were always moving my seat around. Like, not just once or twice — it felt like they were always trying to put me somewhere else because I couldn’t stay put. I’d be up before class was done, or I’d jump out of my seat when I wasn’t supposed to. Sometimes I’d talk out of turn, like I knew I was supposed to wait but it would just come out anyway, and then I’d get in trouble for it.

I remember being told to sit down, be quiet, stop moving, wait until class is over… that kind of thing. So, yeah, when you ask if it was there as a child, I’d say yes. It goes way back.
Do you also have trouble staying focused or feel restless when you’re doing tasks that require you to keep your attention on something for a while, like reading, writing, or working on a project?

Yeah, I do. It happens a lot when somebody is telling me something I’m supposed to hold onto for more than just a second.

Like if we’re talking about ride times — say somebody’s telling me, “Be ready at this time, then we’re going here, then we’re picking up so-and-so,” I’ll be listening at the start. I’m not trying to ignore them. I’ll be looking at them, nodding, thinking I’m getting it. But then somewhere in the middle my mind kind of slips off, and I don’t always notice right away. Then later I realize I missed the part I actually needed, like what time exactly or where I was supposed to be.

Same thing with pantry lists or church plans. If somebody’s going through a list of things, I might catch the first couple things, then it gets blurry. I’ll remember there was something about this person bringing that, or we’re supposed to meet somewhere, but I don’t have the full thing. Then I have to ask again, and I feel bad because I know they already told me.

So yeah, if it’s something that needs me to keep my attention on it for a while, especially listening to instructions or plans, I start out okay but I don’t stay locked in. My mind just kind of wanders off before I mean for it to.
Do you also have trouble staying focused or feel restless in other settings, like when you’re at work or when you’re interacting with friends?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, I’m not working right now, so I can’t really say like “at work” currently, but in other places, yes. It follows me around. It’s not just one place.

That’s honestly a big part of why I came in. I feel like I’ve got this motor running inside me all day. Like even if I’m sitting still on the outside, inside I don’t feel still. I feel like I need to get up, or move, or do something with myself. If I’m at church and I have to sit there for a long stretch, I start feeling trapped, like I’m stuck in the seat. I’ll be shifting around, thinking about standing up, looking for a reason to go do something, even if I know I’m supposed to just sit and listen.

Same thing at the clinic, like waiting in a chair. I can sit there for a little bit, but then it starts building up in me. It’s not even that I’m trying to be rude or impatient. It just feels like my body is saying, “Get up, get up, get up.” And at home it happens too, which is what makes it frustrating, because home is where you’re supposed to relax. But I’ll be sitting there and still feel like I can’t settle, like I need to pop up and do something, even if there’s nothing that really needs doing.

So yeah, around people, out places, or even just at home by myself, that restless feeling is there a lot.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others when they’re talking, acting without thinking about the consequences, or having trouble waiting your turn in situations like conversations or lines?

Yeah… waiting my turn is a big one for me. Lines, especially, or sitting at the doctor’s office waiting to be called back — that gets me worked up fast.

I’ll tell myself, “Just stand here, just wait, everybody has to wait,” but my body doesn’t really listen. I start stepping around, shifting from one foot to the other, looking around, checking the door, watching who gets called before me. And then I’ll start asking, like, “How much longer do you think it’ll be?” or “Am I next?” even when I know they probably already told me to wait.

It’s embarrassing sometimes because I know I look impatient. I’m not trying to make anybody’s job harder. It just builds up in me, like I feel stuck there. At the doctor’s office, if I’m waiting too long, I’ll get up and walk around, go outside for a minute, come back in, ask again. And there have been times where I’ve just left when I really should have stayed, because I couldn’t take sitting there or standing there anymore.

So yeah, waiting my turn is hard. It’s not just annoying to me — it makes me feel all stirred up inside, like I have to do something right then.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting, unable to relax when you need to be quiet, or talking more than you intend to, even when it’s not appropriate?

Yeah, the fidgeting part for sure. Even when I’m trying to be respectful — like I know I’m supposed to sit still and be quiet — my body is still doing something.

My leg will be bouncing without me even deciding to do it. Or I’ll be tapping my fingers on the chair, or rubbing my hands together, or twisting something in my hands if I’ve got anything nearby. Sometimes I don’t even notice at first until somebody looks at me, or I hear the tapping myself and realize I’ve been doing it the whole time.

It’s like I can tell myself, “Just sit still, don’t move around so much,” but then a minute later my foot’s going again, or my fingers are picking at something. I don’t mean it to be distracting or disrespectful. I really don’t. It just feels like if I have to be quiet, some part of me still has to move.
Do you find yourself more restless or unable to stay still in situations where other people are calm and quiet, like in meetings, at the movies, or during meals?

Yeah, that’s exactly when I notice it the most, honestly — when everybody else is calm and sitting still, and I’m supposed to be calm too.

That’s part of why I came in, because it feels like I’ve got this motor running inside me all day. Like my body is sitting there, but inside I’m not settled at all. If I’m somewhere quiet, like church, and people are sitting and listening, I start feeling trapped in the seat. I’ll shift around, lean forward, lean back, look around, try to make myself stay put, but the whole time I’m thinking, “I need to get up. I need to move. I need to do something.”

Same kind of thing happens at the clinic if I’m waiting. Everybody else might be just sitting there normal, reading something or looking at their phone, and I’m over there feeling like I can’t take being in the chair anymore. I’ll feel like I have to stand up or walk around, even if there’s no real reason to.

And even at home, which is frustrating, because there’s no pressure there really. I can be in my own place and still feel like I can’t just relax and sit still. I’ll sit down and then almost right away there’s this feeling like I need to pop up and do something, even if I don’t know what it is. It’s like being still makes me feel boxed in.
Do you often find yourself acting so quickly on urges that you don’t stop to think about the consequences, like saying or doing something before you mean to?

Yeah… yeah, that happens to me a lot, especially with talking. I’ll jump in with an answer before the person is even finished asking or explaining something.

Like at church, if the pastor is saying something or asking something, I’ll think I know where he’s going with it, and I’ll blurt something out too soon. Then he finishes and I realize, oh… that wasn’t even what he was asking, or I answered the wrong thing. And then I feel stupid, because everybody heard me jump in like that.

It happens with my cousin too. He’ll be telling me something, and before he gets the whole sentence out I’m already answering him, like I can’t just wait for the last part. Then sometimes he gets irritated and says, “Man, let me finish,” and I know he’s right. I don’t mean to cut him off. It’s like the answer comes out before I can stop it.

Even at the pantry, with the lady there, she’ll be explaining what I need to do or asking me a question, and I’ll answer before she’s done. Then I realize I answered the wrong thing, or I made her mad because it sounded like I wasn’t listening. I am trying to listen, but I jump ahead in my head and my mouth just goes with it.

And then afterward I’m standing there thinking, why didn’t I just wait two more seconds? But in the moment it feels like it comes out too fast for me to catch it.

Do you often find yourself doing things without thinking them through, like starting a task before you’ve heard all the instructions or making decisions too quickly without considering the consequences?

Yeah… that happens with instructions a lot. Like I’ll think I understand what somebody wants me to do, so I’ll just start moving on it before I really got the whole thing.

If a relative asks me to run an errand, for example, I might hear the first part — like go pick this up, or drop this off — and I’ll go do that part. But there was a second part or another thing they told me, and by the time I’m out doing it, it’s just gone from my head. Then later they’ll ask, “Did you also do the other thing?” and I’m like… no, I didn’t. I’ll realize I never finished the whole errand, just the first piece of it.

Same thing at the pantry sometimes. Somebody will tell me what job they need done, and I’ll get started because I don’t want to look like I’m just standing around. But I’ll do the first thing and then kind of miss the rest of what was expected. Then later somebody notices, like, “Hey, this didn’t get finished,” or “You were supposed to do this after that,” and that’s when it comes out that I only did part of it.

It’s embarrassing because I’m not trying to be lazy or ignore people. In my mind, I started it, so I feel like I was doing what I was supposed to do. But then everybody else sees that I didn’t actually finish the whole thing. And I hate that, because it makes me seem careless, but a lot of the time I just move too fast at the beginning and don’t hold onto all the instructions.
Do these symptoms interfere with your ability to function well in your daily life, such as in school, work, relationships, or other important activities?

Yeah… it really does. I mean, that’s probably the part that bothers me the most, because it’s not just me feeling uncomfortable inside. It’s like it spills over onto everybody around me, and then people stop depending on me.

At church, at the pantry, even in my own family, people don’t really trust me with certain things anymore. Like rides, appointments, picking things up, bringing supplies — stuff where somebody needs me to be on time, remember what I’m supposed to do, and follow through. And I get why they feel that way, I do, because there have been times I meant to help and then I messed it up somehow. But it still hurts.

It’s embarrassing because I’ll say, “Yeah, I can do that,” and I really mean it in the moment. I’m not trying to blow anybody off or make things harder. But then something gets missed, or I don’t handle it the way they expected, and after enough times they start giving those jobs to somebody else. Or they’ll double-check me like they already expect I’m going to forget or mess it up. That makes me feel like a grown man who can’t be counted on.

And with my family, that’s probably the worst feeling. I want to be useful. I want them to feel like, “Okay, he’s got it.” But instead I feel like I keep letting everybody down, even when my intention is to help. So yeah, it affects my day-to-day life a lot. It affects how people see me, and honestly how I see myself too.

And it’s frustrating because it’s not always like I’m walking around or doing something else. I can be right there looking at the person, trying to listen, and still it doesn’t all stay with me.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences symptoms of inattention or distractibility in addition to restlessness, which would help differentiate between ADHD presentations.
doctor.question: Do you often find that you’re not paying close attention to details, or do you make careless mistakes because your mind is somewhere else?

target_item.reason: The question is specifically about poor attention to details or careless mistakes, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles. The closest profile is sustained attention difficulty, but it does not specifically address careless mistakes or overlooking details.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure about that one. I mean, I can say I miss things sometimes, but whether it’s because I’m not paying close attention to details or because my mind is somewhere else… I don’t know if I could separate that out real clear.

Like, if somebody later says, “You didn’t notice that part,” or “That’s not what I said,” I might realize I missed something, but I don’t always know in the moment what happened. I don’t sit there thinking, “Oh, I’m ignoring the details.” It’s more after the fact that I might see I didn’t catch everything.

As far as careless mistakes, I don’t know. I don’t have a good example coming to mind right now. I’m not saying it never happens, but I haven’t really paid attention to it that way, like enough to say yes, that’s a big thing for me.

inference.note: The patient endorses difficulty concentrating and being easily distracted, which supports continuation of ADHD subtypes (F90.0, F90.8, F90.9). The absence of clear reports of racing thoughts, unusual excitement, or manic-like symptoms makes F31.xx (Bipolar Disorders) less likely at this point. Further clarification is needed regarding hyperactivity and impulsivity symptoms to differentiate between ADHD presentations.

doctor.intent: Determine if symptoms are present in multiple settings (e.g., work, school, home, social situations) beyond those already mentioned, to help differentiate between F90.0 (ADHD, Combined Type), F90.8 (ADHD, Other Specified), and F90.9 (ADHD, Unspecified).
doctor.question: Can you tell me if you also have trouble staying focused or feel restless in settings like work, school, or when you’re out with friends, even if you’re not moving around?

target_item.name: Feeling_Restless
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I feel like I got a motor running inside me all day, and if I have to sit still at church, at the clinic, or at home, I feel trapped and have to get up or do something.
target_item.reason: The question asks about feeling restless in settings like work, school, or with friends, even when not physically moving around, which matches the internal restlessness described in this item.

patient.answer:
Yeah… that’s actually kind of the main reason I came in, to be honest. It’s like I’ve got a motor running inside me all day. That’s the best way I can explain it. Even if I’m sitting there and I’m not supposed to be doing anything, inside I don’t feel still. I feel like I need to get up, or shift around, or go do something, or I’m just… stuck in my own skin, if that makes sense.

Like at church, if I have to sit through everything, I start feeling trapped. Not because anything bad is happening, but because sitting there that long feels almost unbearable sometimes. Same thing at the clinic, like waiting around, sitting in the chair, trying to just be patient — I can do it for a little while, but then I start feeling like I’ve got to stand up or move or find some reason to do something.

And at home too, it’s not like it only happens out in public. If I’m just sitting there and I’m supposed to relax, I don’t really relax. I’ll feel that pressure inside, like I need to get up. Even if I’m not physically running around, I still feel restless inside. That’s probably the biggest thing — I don’t feel settled.

doctor.intent: Determine if symptoms are present in childhood, which is required for the diagnosis of ADHD (F90.x).
doctor.question: When did you first start noticing these feelings of restlessness and trouble focusing? Were they present when you were a child, or did they start more recently?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Back when I was a boy in school, teachers were always moving my seat because I could not stay put, talked out of turn, and got in trouble for jumping up before class was done.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking when the symptoms began and whether they were present in childhood, which directly matches onset prior to age 12.

patient.answer:
Yeah, it was definitely there when I was a kid. I don’t think this is something that just started recently. I mean, it feels worse now in some ways because I’m older and there’s more I’m supposed to handle, but when I think back, it was already happening when I was a boy in school.

Teachers were always moving my seat around. Like, not just once or twice — it felt like they were always trying to put me somewhere else because I couldn’t stay put. I’d be up before class was done, or I’d jump out of my seat when I wasn’t supposed to. Sometimes I’d talk out of turn, like I knew I was supposed to wait but it would just come out anyway, and then I’d get in trouble for it.

I remember being told to sit down, be quiet, stop moving, wait until class is over… that kind of thing. So, yeah, when you ask if it was there as a child, I’d say yes. It goes way back.

doctor.intent: Determine if symptoms of inattention and restlessness are present in multiple settings beyond those already discussed, such as during tasks requiring sustained mental effort or in structured activities.
doctor.question: Do you also have trouble staying focused or feel restless when you’re doing tasks that require you to keep your attention on something for a while, like reading, writing, or working on a project?

target_item.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: When folks are talking through ride times, pantry lists, or church plans, I listen good at first, but then my mind slips off and I miss pieces I really needed to hear.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about trouble keeping attention on tasks for a while, such as reading, writing, or working on a project, which directly matches sustained attention difficulty.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I do. It happens a lot when somebody is telling me something I’m supposed to hold onto for more than just a second.

Like if we’re talking about ride times — say somebody’s telling me, “Be ready at this time, then we’re going here, then we’re picking up so-and-so,” I’ll be listening at the start. I’m not trying to ignore them. I’ll be looking at them, nodding, thinking I’m getting it. But then somewhere in the middle my mind kind of slips off, and I don’t always notice right away. Then later I realize I missed the part I actually needed, like what time exactly or where I was supposed to be.

Same thing with pantry lists or church plans. If somebody’s going through a list of things, I might catch the first couple things, then it gets blurry. I’ll remember there was something about this person bringing that, or we’re supposed to meet somewhere, but I don’t have the full thing. Then I have to ask again, and I feel bad because I know they already told me.

So yeah, if it’s something that needs me to keep my attention on it for a while, especially listening to instructions or plans, I start out okay but I don’t stay locked in. My mind just kind of wanders off before I mean for it to.

doctor.intent: Determine if symptoms are present in multiple settings beyond those already discussed (e.g., work, school, social settings) to support a diagnosis of ADHD.
doctor.question: Do you also have trouble staying focused or feel restless in other settings, like when you’re at work or when you’re interacting with friends?

target_item.name: Feeling_Restless
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I feel like I got a motor running inside me all day, and if I have to sit still at church, at the clinic, or at home, I feel trapped and have to get up or do something.
target_item.reason: The question is most directly asking about feeling restless across other settings, and this item covers the internal motor-like restlessness and difficulty staying still in situations where sitting is expected.

patient.answer:
Yeah, definitely. I mean, I’m not working right now, so I can’t really say like “at work” currently, but in other places, yes. It follows me around. It’s not just one place.

That’s honestly a big part of why I came in. I feel like I’ve got this motor running inside me all day. Like even if I’m sitting still on the outside, inside I don’t feel still. I feel like I need to get up, or move, or do something with myself. If I’m at church and I have to sit there for a long stretch, I start feeling trapped, like I’m stuck in the seat. I’ll be shifting around, thinking about standing up, looking for a reason to go do something, even if I know I’m supposed to just sit and listen.

Same thing at the clinic, like waiting in a chair. I can sit there for a little bit, but then it starts building up in me. It’s not even that I’m trying to be rude or impatient. It just feels like my body is saying, “Get up, get up, get up.” And at home it happens too, which is what makes it frustrating, because home is where you’re supposed to relax. But I’ll be sitting there and still feel like I can’t settle, like I need to pop up and do something, even if there’s nothing that really needs doing.

So yeah, around people, out places, or even just at home by myself, that restless feeling is there a lot.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences symptoms of impulsivity, such as interrupting others, difficulty waiting their turn, or acting without thinking, which are key features of ADHD and can help distinguish between the remaining diagnostic candidates.
doctor.question: Do you often find yourself interrupting others when they’re talking, acting without thinking about the consequences, or having trouble waiting your turn in situations like conversations or lines?

target_item.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: Waiting my turn in lines or at the doctor’s office makes me so worked up that I keep stepping around, asking how much longer, and sometimes I just walk off when I should stay.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking most directly about having trouble waiting your turn, especially in conversations or lines.

patient.answer:
Yeah… waiting my turn is a big one for me. Lines, especially, or sitting at the doctor’s office waiting to be called back — that gets me worked up fast.

I’ll tell myself, “Just stand here, just wait, everybody has to wait,” but my body doesn’t really listen. I start stepping around, shifting from one foot to the other, looking around, checking the door, watching who gets called before me. And then I’ll start asking, like, “How much longer do you think it’ll be?” or “Am I next?” even when I know they probably already told me to wait.

It’s embarrassing sometimes because I know I look impatient. I’m not trying to make anybody’s job harder. It just builds up in me, like I feel stuck there. At the doctor’s office, if I’m waiting too long, I’ll get up and walk around, go outside for a minute, come back in, ask again. And there have been times where I’ve just left when I really should have stayed, because I couldn’t take sitting there or standing there anymore.

So yeah, waiting my turn is hard. It’s not just annoying to me — it makes me feel all stirred up inside, like I have to do something right then.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has symptoms of hyperactivity or impulsivity that are not already covered by restlessness, such as fidgeting, inability to play quietly, or excessive talking.
doctor.question: Do you often find yourself fidgeting, unable to relax when you need to be quiet, or talking more than you intend to, even when it’s not appropriate?

target_item.name: Fidgeting
target_item.manifestation: Even when I’m trying to be respectful, my leg is bouncing, my fingers are tapping the chair, or I’m twisting something in my hands the whole time.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking most directly about fidgeting and difficulty staying still or quiet, which matches this symptom.

patient.answer:
Yeah, the fidgeting part for sure. Even when I’m trying to be respectful — like I know I’m supposed to sit still and be quiet — my body is still doing something.

My leg will be bouncing without me even deciding to do it. Or I’ll be tapping my fingers on the chair, or rubbing my hands together, or twisting something in my hands if I’ve got anything nearby. Sometimes I don’t even notice at first until somebody looks at me, or I hear the tapping myself and realize I’ve been doing it the whole time.

It’s like I can tell myself, “Just sit still, don’t move around so much,” but then a minute later my foot’s going again, or my fingers are picking at something. I don’t mean it to be distracting or disrespectful. I really don’t. It just feels like if I have to be quiet, some part of me still has to move.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences symptoms of hyperactivity or excessive restlessness specifically in situations where others are typically calm and quiet, to help differentiate between ADHD presentations.
doctor.question: Do you find yourself more restless or unable to stay still in situations where other people are calm and quiet, like in meetings, at the movies, or during meals?

target_item.name: Feeling_Restless
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I feel like I got a motor running inside me all day, and if I have to sit still at church, at the clinic, or at home, I feel trapped and have to get up or do something.
target_item.reason: The question is most directly asking about feeling restless or unable to stay still in calm, quiet situations.

patient.answer:
Yeah, that’s exactly when I notice it the most, honestly — when everybody else is calm and sitting still, and I’m supposed to be calm too.

That’s part of why I came in, because it feels like I’ve got this motor running inside me all day. Like my body is sitting there, but inside I’m not settled at all. If I’m somewhere quiet, like church, and people are sitting and listening, I start feeling trapped in the seat. I’ll shift around, lean forward, lean back, look around, try to make myself stay put, but the whole time I’m thinking, “I need to get up. I need to move. I need to do something.”

Same kind of thing happens at the clinic if I’m waiting. Everybody else might be just sitting there normal, reading something or looking at their phone, and I’m over there feeling like I can’t take being in the chair anymore. I’ll feel like I have to stand up or walk around, even if there’s no real reason to.

And even at home, which is frustrating, because there’s no pressure there really. I can be in my own place and still feel like I can’t just relax and sit still. I’ll sit down and then almost right away there’s this feeling like I need to pop up and do something, even if I don’t know what it is. It’s like being still makes me feel boxed in.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences symptoms of hyperactivity-impulsivity that are not captured by restlessness alone, which would help differentiate between ADHD presentations and other diagnoses.
doctor.question: Do you often find yourself acting so quickly on urges that you don’t stop to think about the consequences, like saying or doing something before you mean to?

target_item.name: Blurting_Answers
target_item.manifestation: I jump in with an answer before the pastor, my cousin, or the pantry lady is done talking, and then I realize I answered the wrong thing or made them mad.
target_item.reason: The question is most directly about acting on urges by saying something before intending to, which matches blurting out answers before others finish speaking.

patient.answer:
Yeah… yeah, that happens to me a lot, especially with talking. I’ll jump in with an answer before the person is even finished asking or explaining something.

Like at church, if the pastor is saying something or asking something, I’ll think I know where he’s going with it, and I’ll blurt something out too soon. Then he finishes and I realize, oh… that wasn’t even what he was asking, or I answered the wrong thing. And then I feel stupid, because everybody heard me jump in like that.

It happens with my cousin too. He’ll be telling me something, and before he gets the whole sentence out I’m already answering him, like I can’t just wait for the last part. Then sometimes he gets irritated and says, “Man, let me finish,” and I know he’s right. I don’t mean to cut him off. It’s like the answer comes out before I can stop it.

Even at the pantry, with the lady there, she’ll be explaining what I need to do or asking me a question, and I’ll answer before she’s done. Then I realize I answered the wrong thing, or I made her mad because it sounded like I wasn’t listening. I am trying to listen, but I jump ahead in my head and my mouth just goes with it.

And then afterward I’m standing there thinking, why didn’t I just wait two more seconds? But in the moment it feels like it comes out too fast for me to catch it.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences symptoms of hyperactivity-impulsivity in addition to restlessness and inattention, which would support a diagnosis of ADHD (F90.x).
doctor.question: Do you often find yourself doing things without thinking them through, like starting a task before you’ve heard all the instructions or making decisions too quickly without considering the consequences?

target_item.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: I’ll start an errand for my relative or a job at the pantry, but I end up doing the first part and then forget the rest, so people find out later that I never finished it.
target_item.reason: The question is most directly asking about starting tasks before fully taking in instructions and then not completing or following through properly.

patient.answer:
Yeah… that happens with instructions a lot. Like I’ll think I understand what somebody wants me to do, so I’ll just start moving on it before I really got the whole thing.

If a relative asks me to run an errand, for example, I might hear the first part — like go pick this up, or drop this off — and I’ll go do that part. But there was a second part or another thing they told me, and by the time I’m out doing it, it’s just gone from my head. Then later they’ll ask, “Did you also do the other thing?” and I’m like… no, I didn’t. I’ll realize I never finished the whole errand, just the first piece of it.

Same thing at the pantry sometimes. Somebody will tell me what job they need done, and I’ll get started because I don’t want to look like I’m just standing around. But I’ll do the first thing and then kind of miss the rest of what was expected. Then later somebody notices, like, “Hey, this didn’t get finished,” or “You were supposed to do this after that,” and that’s when it comes out that I only did part of it.

It’s embarrassing because I’m not trying to be lazy or ignore people. In my mind, I started it, so I feel like I was doing what I was supposed to do. But then everybody else sees that I didn’t actually finish the whole thing. And I hate that, because it makes me seem careless, but a lot of the time I just move too fast at the beginning and don’t hold onto all the instructions.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient's symptoms cause clinically significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning, which is necessary to distinguish between F90.0 (ADHD, Combined Type), F90.8 (ADHD, Other Specified), and F90.9 (ADHD, Unspecified).
doctor.question: Do these symptoms interfere with your ability to function well in your daily life, such as in school, work, relationships, or other important activities?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: People at church, the pantry, and in my family have stopped trusting me with rides, appointments, and supplies, and I feel like I keep letting everybody down even when I mean to help.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the symptoms interfere with daily functioning in areas like relationships, work, or important activities, which directly matches functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yeah… it really does. I mean, that’s probably the part that bothers me the most, because it’s not just me feeling uncomfortable inside. It’s like it spills over onto everybody around me, and then people stop depending on me.

At church, at the pantry, even in my own family, people don’t really trust me with certain things anymore. Like rides, appointments, picking things up, bringing supplies — stuff where somebody needs me to be on time, remember what I’m supposed to do, and follow through. And I get why they feel that way, I do, because there have been times I meant to help and then I messed it up somehow. But it still hurts.

It’s embarrassing because I’ll say, “Yeah, I can do that,” and I really mean it in the moment. I’m not trying to blow anybody off or make things harder. But then something gets missed, or I don’t handle it the way they expected, and after enough times they start giving those jobs to somebody else. Or they’ll double-check me like they already expect I’m going to forget or mess it up. That makes me feel like a grown man who can’t be counted on.

And with my family, that’s probably the worst feeling. I want to be useful. I want them to feel like, “Okay, he’s got it.” But instead I feel like I keep letting everybody down, even when my intention is to help. So yeah, it affects my day-to-day life a lot. It affects how people see me, and honestly how I see myself too.

These symptoms are present across multiple settings (e.g., home, church, clinic), began in childhood, and result in significant functional impairment, consistent with ADHD, predominantly combined presentation.
